visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) A woman with long reddish-brown hair, wearing a black sleeveless dress, stands in a professional recording studio. She is seen putting on a pair of large headphones over her ears while a black grand piano sits in the background under warm indoor lighting. (2) She approaches a professional condenser microphone mounted on a shock mount and begins vocalizing with an exaggerated, wide-mouthed expression, looking directly toward the camera. (3) She starts tapping and hitting the microphone grille with her open palm, asking if there is sound. (4) The camera cuts to a man in a green t-shirt sitting at a digital audio workstation in a control room, looking extremely distressed and frustrated as he observes the recording booth. (5) The man shouts angrily, gesturing with his hand for the woman to leave. (6) The video ends with a shot of the woman looking sheepish and sad at the microphone as red warning text and graphical glitch effects appear on the screen.

audio_base.audio_narrative_log: (1) The audio begins with a high-energy, upbeat electronic synth sequence with a driving beat. No vocals are present. (2) A female voice enters with high-intensity vocalizing ('Woah~'), exhibiting significant pitch variability and a clear, bright spectral profile. (3) Frequent percussive thudding sounds interrupt the mix as the mic is physically tapped, followed by a loud, high-arousal female voice shouting '1 2 1 2'. (4) The BGM shifts abruptly as a male voice enters with extreme intensity and aggression, shouting 'How could you do this to expensive equipment!' in Traditional Chinese. (5) A sharp 'crack' or slap sound effect occurs simultaneously with the male shouting. (6) The male voice commands the other person to get out with high dominance and strain. (7) The video concludes with digital glitch sound effects and a final comedic synthesizer stinger.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: To humorously illustrate a major 'taboo' in professional recording environments: hitting the microphone. The video uses exaggerated character reactions and meme-style editing to warn viewers against improper handling of studio equipment.

high_inference.freeDescribe: The video effectively combines comedic timing with relatable professional stress in a studio setting.
